executive_assessment.text: The World Bank summary says sea-level rise threatens coastlines on which much of Cabo Verde’s tourism depends.
The summary identifies drought and saline intrusion as threats to agriculture, income and food security in rural communities of this water-scarce country.

The World Bank reports that hazard and climate-risk assessments were incorporated into municipal spatial-planning tools and that a Ministry of Finance risk service and National Emergency Fund were operationalized.

geographic_notes.text: Rural and peri-urban Cabo Verde: The NDC says rural and peri-urban women in agriculture, water management and care face higher workloads and reduced income during prolonged drought and resource scarcity, while remaining underrepresented in climate governance.

known_gaps.text: No full CCDR PDF was inspected; the 2025 World Bank publisher summary does not disclose projection assumptions.
The NDC’s differentiated vulnerability statements were not independently triangulated with subnational data.

The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
